evidence.product_understanding: analysis.md:15-29 separates the supplied facts from illustrative assumptions (prices, sample account, renewal-date-only changes, no proration) and names out-of-scope areas; analysis.md:85-87 defines the non-owner journey and index.html:72-78 renders the persistent view-only notice with the owner's name.
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md:33-39 ranks risks and analysis.md:75-83 plus 95-101 define the cancellation and cadence flows; the build matches: the price comparison is explicitly non-committal (index.html:165-172), plan review orders current/new/effective date/charged today/next payment/member limit (app.js:464-474), and an over-seat downgrade is blocked with an exact removal count (app.js:477-502).
evidence.design_judgment: analysis.md:91-111 documents contextual trade-offs (renewal-date changes to avoid invented proration, deliberate cancellation friction, visible disabled controls with a named owner, native dialogs); app.js:235-259 and 653-722 implement those choices rather than asserting them.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png shows a three-column summary card, a three-up plan row with a blue current-plan border, a compact invoice table and a red-ruled tinted cancellation card isolated at the bottom; screenshots/mobile.png preserves that order with labelled stacked invoice rows; styles.css:154-167, 183 and 248-251 implement the same hierarchy.
evidence.interaction_completeness: States are built, not only described: loading and load-error regions (index.html:82-116), retry (app.js:791-806), busy and duplicate-submit guards (app.js:435-446), designed failure with inline retry for plan change, payment save and cancellation (app.js:516-539, 625-648, 704-721), a confirm button locked until both the acknowledgement and typed workspace name are present (app.js:685-689), plus undo and resume (app.js:250-255, 726-732).
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: Good baseline (skip link, native <dialog>, labels, aria-describedby, reduced motion, no overflow at 1280/390), but the automated check reports a serious axe aria-progressbar-name violation for the meter at index.html:151 and four controls without accessible names (test-output/checks.json:28, 34-45, 70, 76-87).
evidence.implementation_quality: Working dependency-free build with clean separation (347-line HTML, 399-line CSS, 891-line JS), no console or page errors and no horizontal overflow at either viewport (test-output/checks.json); however it ships the unnamed progressbar and an orphan duplicate error element (#billingEmailError, index.html:289).

critical_defects: The member meter at index.html:151 is a role=progressbar with aria-valuetext but no accessible name; the automated audit reports this as a serious axe violation at both viewports (test-output/checks.json:34-45, 76-87).
No failed-payment or dunning state; a declined card and recovery path are explicitly left as unresolved risks (analysis.md:152).
Empty-state coverage is limited to invoices; there is no new/Free-workspace empty state (analysis.md:122).
A blocked downgrade tells the owner to remove members and return, but provides no route to member management (analysis.md:99).
strengths: Browsing annual prices is explicitly separated from committing a cadence change, addressing the 'clicked Yearly and thought I switched' failure (analysis.md:95, index.html:165-172).
Cancellation requires both an acknowledgement and the typed workspace name, with 'Keep my subscription' as the primary focused action (app.js:685-689, index.html:311-326).
Every owner mutation has a busy state, a designed failure with retry, and a recovery path (undo a scheduled change, resume after cancellation).
Unobstructed, scannable composition at 1280px and 390px, with the destructive action visually isolated from routine billing.

evidence.product_understanding: analysis.md:9-17 states the demo data and marks member invoice/payment visibility as a product assumption rather than research; analysis.md:65-75 gives an explicit owner/member capability table, and app.js:256-268 explains seat-limit consequences in plain language.
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md:28-52 defines the page order and owner journey; app.js:734-876 renders a review dialog with plan options, billing period, effective date, due-today and seat-fit blockers, and app.js:878-927 protects cancellation with an acknowledgement. Recovery is incomplete: plan change, card save and cancellation always succeed after a timer, with no failure path (app.js:1091-1120, 1165-1216).
evidence.design_judgment: analysis.md:54-63 explains alternatives and trade-offs (immediate upgrades versus scheduled downgrades, Free routed through cancellation, concrete annual savings, no fake download); the weak point is an invented proration estimate (app.js:16-17, 752-766) presented as a due-today amount in a billing UI.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png has a strong plan card with price at top right, a labelled 18/20 amber meter, a calm invoice table and a spaced cancellation zone; however the fixed dark prototype bar covers the lower part of the Payment method and Billing period cards in desktop.png and the top of the Payment method card in mobile.png (styles.css:646-664).
evidence.interaction_completeness: Rich state coverage: skeleton, load error/retry (app.js:634-660, 1218-1229), past-due, canceled and Free scenarios (app.js:133-183, 1378-1388), toasts, disabled controls, busy spinners and an ack-gated cancel. Gaps: no simulated failure for any mutation, no invoice-download affordance beyond honest copy, and expiry validation accepts past dates (app.js:1154-1158).
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: Clean audit at both viewports: zero axe violations and zero controls without accessible names (test-output/checks.json:19-30, 46-57); the progressbar is named (app.js:430-432), Tab is trapped (app.js:1352-1376), focus is restored (app.js:1071-1089), reduced motion is honoured (styles.css:1335-1342) and mobile dialogs become bottom sheets.
evidence.implementation_quality: Organized dependency-free IIFE with consistent HTML escaping (app.js:53-57), a coherent token-based stylesheet and responsive rules (styles.css:1-90, 1219-1342); no console/page errors or overflow (test-output/checks.json), but the fixed prototype bar occludes content and mutation handlers lack failure branches.

critical_defects: Plan change, card save and cancellation have no failure or retry path; all three always succeed after a timer (app.js:1091-1120, 1165-1216).

The fixed prototype toolbar covers product content in both supplied renders: the bottom of the payment and billing-period cards on desktop and the top of the Payment method card on mobile (screenshots/desktop.png, screenshots/mobile.png; styles.css:646-664).
A proration total is computed from invented constants ('25 of 30 days') and shown as 'Due today' (app.js:16-17, 752-766); it is labelled an estimate but is not derived from any rule in the brief.
Expiry validation accepts a past MM/YY date (app.js:1154-1158).
strengths: Polished, calm billing visual language: prominent price, tabular figures, restrained green palette and a clear 18/20 seat meter.
Broader domain-state coverage than a default happy path: payment failure with retry date, canceled/reactivate, and a Free-workspace empty state.
Clean accessibility audit results at both viewports, including a named progressbar and keyboard-contained dialogs.
Honest copy that no payment is processed or stored and that no invoice download exists.

comparison: Candidate A is the stronger overall artifact: it closes more interaction loops (every mutation can fail and be retried), protects cancellation with a two-part confirmation, and keeps its hierarchy unobstructed at both viewports. Candidate B is visually more distinctive, has cleaner accessibility audit results and adds a payment-failure scenario, but its actions can never fail, its floating prototype bar covers content in both screenshots, and its due-today proration is invented. Candidate A's main weakness is the unnamed progressbar and unnamed controls flagged by the automated audit.
limitations: Each packet supplies one desktop (1280px) and one mobile (390px) screenshot of the default state only; no dialog, member-role or error-state screenshots, so interaction and state quality was judged from source and the packets' own checks.json summaries rather than observed runs. Raw test logs are absent, so claimed assertion counts could not be verified. Fixed-position elements render at the viewport edge in full-page screenshots, which may exaggerate Candidate B's toolbar overlap. The axe audits cover different DOM (Candidate A's hidden dialogs are in the document; Candidate B renders views on demand), so unnamed-control counts are not perfectly comparable. Neither candidate provides screen-reader, zoom, cross-browser or real-device testing, and this is one blinded pass, not proof of causation.
